open_points.subject: recovery status when ready and waiting elements coexist
open_points.text: “A run derived `running` is advanced with `runs`' own advance, which reaches every ready element while other elements still wait …; a run derived still waiting is not advanced” contradicts M19's “its status is `awaiting_approval` when any of them waits, otherwise `pending`.”
open_points.question: When a recovered run has both a waiting element and another ready element, does `run_graph` derive the persisted run status as waiting or return an internal runnable plan distinct from that status, and must `runs` advance it?
options: Derive an internal runnable plan and advance all ready work; persist a waiting status only after no ready work remains
Derive `awaiting_approval` or `pending` whenever any element waits, but still separately tell `runs` to advance ready work
Treat the run as waiting and do not advance any ready work
open_points.default_guess: Use a runnable plan distinct from the persisted status, advance every ready element under A13 rule 8, then persist the final waiting status once no ready element remains.
open_points.unit: 30_modules.md:Facts several modules touch, and their one owner

open_points.subject: recovery precedence for decided approval or resolved not-applied attempt
open_points.text: “an element whose approval the owner approved … or whose attempt the owner resolved `not_applied`, is not reached and so is ready” does not say what happens when later records already conclude the element or establish a fresh `owner_approval` wait.
open_points.question: What record precedence must `effects.operation_element_conclusion` apply when an approved approval or resolved `not_applied` attempt is followed, before the crash, by a concluding NodeExecution or by a newly requested approval?
options: Newest applicable records win: a concluded NodeExecution concludes the element, and a fresh requested approval keeps it waiting
The earlier approved or resolved record always makes the element ready again
Recovery refuses the inconsistent-looking record combination
open_points.default_guess: Derive from the complete record history: concluded NodeExecutions take precedence, then an unresolved fresh requested approval yields `owner_approval`, and only an approved decision or resolved `not_applied` with no later conclusion or fresh request makes the element ready.
